_meta.disclaimer: Educational schematic. Not a patient-specific simulation, not a validated prediction of disease progression, and not a diagnostic tool.

steps.caption: Stage A — entorhinal cortex (anterior parahippocampal gyrus): early tau pathology.
Stage B — hippocampus becomes involved; difficulty forming new memories.
Stage C — lateral temporal and parietal association cortex, precuneus and posterior cingulate.
Stage D — frontal association cortex; primary motor, sensory and visual cortex relatively spared until late.

animations.title: Nigrostriatal dopamine loss and basal ganglia circuitry

steps.caption: The substantia nigra pars compacta lies within the cerebral peduncle region (not separately segmented — schematic).
Nigrostriatal neurons project dopamine to the striatum — most importantly the putamen.
Reduced dopamine alters output from the globus pallidus to the thalamus…
…and thalamocortical drive to motor cortex, producing slowness and rigidity.

animations.title: Conceptual middle cerebral artery territory ischaemia

steps.caption: Normal perfusion (vessels not modelled).
An embolus blocks the left middle cerebral artery: the core (deep structures) is affected first.
Surrounding cortex in the MCA territory is at risk (penumbra) — potentially salvageable with rapid treatment.
Result: right-sided weakness and sensory loss; language impairment is likely when the dominant (usually left) hemisphere is affected.
Focal onset in the left hippocampus (example of a common focus).
Spread within the medial temporal network: amygdala and parahippocampal gyrus (aura, impaired awareness).
Spread to lateral temporal and insular cortex.
Possible propagation via thalamus to both hemispheres (focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizure).

animations.title: Illustrative frontal lesion with mass effect

steps.caption: An illustrative lesion is placed in the right frontal white matter. Real tumours vary in location, shape and infiltration.
As the lesion and surrounding oedema grow, neighbouring structures are pushed away (mass effect).
Infiltrating tumours can spread along white matter, including across the corpus callosum.

animations.title: Illustrative extra-axial lesion compressing the brain

steps.caption: Meningiomas arise from the meninges, outside brain tissue. Illustrative convexity lesion over the left frontal lobe.
Slow growth compresses the underlying cortex rather than invading it.

animations.title: Demyelination along an axon (separate microscopic schematic)

steps.caption: A healthy myelinated axon: impulses jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction).
Immune cells attack myelin, creating a focal demyelinated segment.
Conduction slows or fails across the damaged segment; the axon itself may later be injured.
Partial remyelination can occur, often with thinner myelin.

animations.note: Demyelination is microscopic. It is NOT visible as a change in a whole lobe; the 3D view shows typical lesion locations only.
